_howto: Newest first. Add an entry at the top each time you push an update; the website and the in-game 'What's new' both read this file. tag: new | improved | fixed.

items.text: The stadium crowd reacts with pixel emoji over their heads: 😱 at wrecks, 🦘📸 when you hit wildlife, 😠👎 for dirty driving, 😂🔥 for a good sledge, 🔥👏 when you take the lead, and a wall of 🎉🏆 when you win.

New art on the radio: your #8 helmet when you talk back, a burst of static as each call connects, and more crew faces (Rosa pleased with a repair, June cheering when you lead or win, Gazza happy or furious about his bet).
Barry Doolan's lower-third now uses a proper Channel 8 frame, and he gets excited for crashes, wildlife hits and sledges.
The TALK button on phones has its own walkie-talkie art and a pressed state. It's the same size and in the same place as before.
Grudges get a red angry-face badge in the garage and on the grid.
Head-to-head records: the garage shows how you stack up against each rival this season ("You lead 3–1", "Duke leads 2–0").
Grudges show in the garage too ("Hasn’t forgotten your sledge at Red Centre"). If a rival with a grudge lines up beside you, they bring it up on the grid.
The results screen replays the radio moment of the race: your best sledge and the comeback, or the last word from a rival at the flag.
The season ending now gives your rivals a closing line, based on how you did against them: "Duke Vance never beat you once all season. He’s still trying to work out how."

Hitting a wallaby or emu now plays only the new explosion art: an impact fireball with a feather burst for emus or a dust ring for wallabies, centred where you hit it. The old dot particles and the doubled crash flash are gone.
If two trucks hit the same animal at once, you see one explosion, not two. The animal also no longer flashes on screen for a frame after it's hit.

Talk back! When a rival gets on the radio, press T (LB on a controller, or tap the TALK button on phones) to answer. Sledge them for $15 and a roar from the crowd, but they'll come hunting you. If they're a mate, it's friendly banter instead.
Rivals hold grudges. Ram someone, mouth off at them, or finish right next to them, and they'll bring it up next race: "Still sore about Kakadu, rookie."
Barry Doolan's commentary now shows up as a Channel 8 TV lower-third, with his face, a name tab and a LIVE tag.
Your rivals talk a lot more now. They gloat when they pass you, laugh when you spin out, swear when they wreck, taunt you on the last lap, and have something to say at the finish line.
Your crew is on the radio. June spots for you: which side a roo or emu is coming from, wrecks up ahead, when you take the lead. Rosa calls in when the truck is getting knocked about.
Paddock deals come back on race day. Bet a rival and they'll remind you about it, Sal has heard about the envelope, and if you bet with Gazza he'll sweat every place you gain or lose.
Radio pop-ups slide in with a burst of static and type out their line. Faces change with the mood (smug, angry, shocked), and the Yowie growls instead of beeping.
Hit a wallaby or an emu and it goes up in a big cartoon fireball: a starburst, rolling flames, a ring of fur or feathers, then a cloud of red-dirt dust. KA-BOING!
A cleaner Channel 8 LIVE bug in the top-right corner, with a blinking red dot.
Outline buttons on the menus now have a purple background so they’re easier to see.

notes.title: Cloud saves, weekly challenge, trophies and Season 2

items.text: Cloud saves: sign in with your name and PIN and your season, money, crew and trophies follow you between your phone and computer. If two devices disagree, you pick which season to keep.

Weekly challenge: one featured track a week, best single lap in the standard truck. When the week closes on Monday (midnight UTC), the top three take gold, silver and bronze for their medal shelf. Chase the leader’s ghost.
Trophy cabinet: 18 trophies to chase across every season, from “Roo spotter” and “Nitro junkie” to “Clean hands” and “Unmasked”.
Season 2 (and beyond): carry your truck, crew, money and half your reputation into a tougher season. Rivals are faster, Duke remembers how last season went, and the fallout from 1994 plays out.
Gamepad support: Xbox, PlayStation or Switch Pro controllers drive, pause and work the menus.
Settings: steering sensitivity, screen shake (full, less or off), controls and sound in one place.
The grid now lines up in the order of the last race: the winner starts on pole, and the rival in the grid moment is whoever is actually lined up beside you.
Wreck parts slid down the screen after they landed. They now stay exactly where they fall until someone drives over them or they blink out.
Driving over a wreck part now catches anywhere under your truck, not just dead centre, so parts break up and slow you as they should.

notes.title: The paddock, and the truth about ’94

items.text: The paddock: between races, walk among whoever’s hanging around tonight and pick three conversations. You can’t talk to everyone.

Paddock talks with Big Earl, Shazza, Thommo, Tash, Sal, Duke and promoter Marge Quill, plus Gazza, Lou and Pemberton. Bet a rival you’ll beat them, buy telemetry, start a feud for the cameras, or shout a tired veteran a flat white.

The 1994 mystery unfolds: June recognises Vance Motors’ chief engineer, the Yowie kneels at Hank’s Corner, Rosa finds a bent steering rack in her dad’s shed, Earl finally talks, and Rick Vance turns up at the benefit with an envelope.
The night before the Showdown, decide who to tell: Channel 8 (a packed, roaring house), Duke (he races you clean), the Yowie (he gives you room), or nobody.
Every rival (and the Yowie) is always around the paddock for a quick word: a compliment, a $50 bet or some trash talk. Their mood shows on their face.
The end-of-season story now remembers what you did about 1994, and whether Gazza ever got his bore pump fixed.

Meet Gazza Reid, the Yowie’s “manager”: lend him money, dob him in, or ask the wrong question about who’s under the helmet. Later he runs a book behind the dunnies, and one night the Yowie’s helmet slips.
Side bets and dirty jobs that play out on race day: put $200 on yourself for a podium, or take the windbreakers’ envelope to put Sal in the wall. Sal finds out.
Lou Tran, Channel 8’s pit reporter, sticks a mic in your face after a podium, digs into the 1994 crash, and might show you crossover-cam footage of Shazza punting you.
Get a nickname from Barry, and he’ll use it when you take the lead or find the scenery.
Drive dirty and Chief Steward Pemberton comes calling: start the next race on penalty points, argue it, or slip him an envelope so the Stewards look the other way for two races.
Faces for Barry Doolan, Chief Steward Pemberton, Biscuit the heeler, Gazza, Lou Tran and the Windbreakers, plus new moods for Rosa, Dex, June and Hank.
Chief Steward Pemberton gets on the radio when the Stewards come for you or wave the black flag.
Barry's face is on the Channel 8 ticker, and every so often he reads a word from the sponsors.
Sponsor billboards around the tracks: Kanga Tyres, Emu Lager, Tin Roo Racing Fuel, Bushfire Motor Oil and more (all made up).
Story scenes can show two faces: Dex with the Windbreakers on his back, Rosa fuming with Hank in the frame. Hank, June and Dex now show their own moods in their scenes.
The fans nearest a wreck throw up a “!!!” before they cheer.
Blond Duke gets a full set of moods (cocky, grinning, snarling, smug, sulking and shocked), and so does the Yowie in his goggles and racing harness.
New portraits for Rosa, Dex, June and Hank. Dex and June now show their faces in their story scenes.
The finale shows the Yowie in his harness before the helmet comes off, then Hank as he is today next to his 1994 archive photo.
A walkie-talkie sits in the corner of the rival radio box during races.
Original music made right in the game: “Billabong Sunset” on the menus and “Red Dirt Run” in races, with didgeridoo, clapsticks, a pub-rock chug and a chiptune lead.
Aussie 8 is dedicated to Ivan “Ironman” Stewart and Super Off Road, the arcade classic that inspired it.
Sign in arcade style with a name and a four-digit PIN, the same way as Typlympics. It works on any device.
Online leaderboards for every track: Best Laps from Time Trial and Best Races from your season races.
Time Trial: four laps in a standard truck against the clock, chasing the ghost of the fastest driver on the board or your own best. Every lap shows how far ahead of or behind the ghost you are.
Race friends live: make a room, share the 4-letter code or link, and race up to 8 people at once. The host picks the track and can fill empty spots with the season's rivals.
The Aussie 8 logo now heads the in-game menu too.

Sound! A growling V8 that revs with your speed and roars on nitro, tyre scrub in the slides, the pack rumbling past, crunching crashes, wall thumps, landings, pickups, the countdown, roos, Stewards sirens and a crowd that cheers, gasps and boos with the race. All made live in the browser.
Sound settings on the menu (effects and music volume), and M mutes during a race.
Fewer crashes: it now takes a harder, more side-on hit to wreck, Grit makes your ute tougher still, and crashes spin you for less time.
Wreck parts on the track slow down whoever drives over them, then break apart. Parts nobody hits blink out after about 25 seconds, so the track no longer fills up.
A badly damaged ute loses a little top speed and weaves slightly. Grab a spanner to straighten it out.
Duke is now the blond champion with the sunglasses.
Every track now has race-day set pieces outside the walls: a race-control tower, gazebos, floodlight towers, Aussie flags, a TV camera crane and roo warning signs.
More trackside clutter: barrier blocks, red, white and black tyre stacks, hay bales, oil drums and cones.
New, bigger nitro (lightning bolt) and repair (spanner) pickups that are easier to spot.

notes.title: A crowd that reacts, and Uluru on every course

items.text: Packed grandstands above every track, with a live crowd in the style of NHL '94. Fans jump up for overtakes and lead changes, lean on the rail for close racing and wrecks, flash cameras at big jumps and kangaroos, boo when the Stewards come out, wave flags on the final lap and go wild when you win.
Reactions ripple out from where the action happened, and the section of crowd nearest the trucks gets on its feet. Every so often a Mexican wave rolls across the stands.
Uluru at sunset is now the backdrop on all eight courses, framed between the two grandstands, with a Channel 8 camera and banner trackside.
On phones the score bar at the top is see-through, so you can see the crowd behind it.
New animated FINAL LAP! and RACE FINISHED! announcements, centred over the track.
New Aussie 8 logo in the website and game headers.
The pause screen text sat off to the left. It's centred now.

notes.title: The art library and Road Rash rivals

items.text: New overhead truck art for all eight drivers, with damage that builds up on the truck over a couple of seconds after each hit. Badly damaged trucks smoke.
Wreck debris: tyres, bumpers, glass and oil fly off in crashes and stay on the track for the rest of the race.
Animated crashes, nitro flames, mud spray, water splashes and drift dust, plus kangaroos and emus that leap clear when clipped.
Rivals remember you. Each driver's opinion of you and their temperament decide whether they give you room, block you or hunt you down.
SHUNT (E or X, or the SHUNT button on phones) bumps the truck beside you. Dirty driving brings out the Stewards' ute and a black flag.
Radio banter from rivals mid-race, and a grid moment before every race: taunt, encourage or ignore the driver beside you.
Channel 8 coverage: live bug, starting grid and final lap graphics, and Barry Doolan on the ticker.
Illustrated story events, location backdrops, character portraits and all six season endings.
The Yowie races #6 as the hardest driver in the field. Beat him in the final round and he takes off the helmet.
Each track has its own skyline and scenery, and every crossover carries the gold ring of Hank's Corner.
On narrow phones in portrait, BRAKE could start a steering drag. Every pedal button now sits fully on the pedal side.
Races go fullscreen on phones, with the controls in the space beside the track so your thumbs don't cover the action.
Drag to steer: put your thumb down anywhere on the left and point where you want the truck to go. Gas is automatic.
Buttons mode for players who prefer it: big ◀ ▶ on the left, and GAS with NITRO right beside it so you can roll your thumb across.
Left-handed option that swaps the steering and pedal sides.
NITRO is bigger and sits right under your thumb. BRAKE moves into the side margin in landscape.
Larger lap, position and nitro readouts on phones, plus vibration on crashes where the phone supports it.
Trucks can now pivot away from a wall while you're on the gas instead of getting pinned.
Aussie 8 has a home page, with these dev notes and a What's new panel in the game.
The season now alternates four regular loops with four figure-8s, finishing on the Outback Showdown figure-8.
The countdown and the garage tell you whether the next track is a loop or a figure-8.
Eight trucks per race. New rivals: Shazza Kelly, Tash Kowalski, Thommo Price and Gazza Reid.
Eight unique tracks, each checked so the only place the two halves meet is the crossover.
Crashes: a hard side-on hit spins both trucks out with sparks, flying paint and screen shake.
Points and prize money now pay all eight places: 10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
The scoreboard shows all eight positions, with yours outlined in gold.
The game is now Aussie 8, with a new arcade title screen.
32-bit pixel art: hand-made truck sprites in 32 directions, dithered red-dirt tracks, tyre walls in green and gold, and Uluru at dusk behind the grandstands.
Kangaroos hop across the track. Clip one and you lose speed; the roo just bounces away.
The story moves to the outback: Coober Pedy, Broken Hill, the Gold Coast, utes, roadhouses and a meat pie sponsor.
Arcade off-road racing with nitro, mud, water, jumps and cash pickups. First released as Backroad Stakes.
RPG garage: driver levels, four stats and truck upgrades.
Good, shady and gamble choices between races, a karma meter and a rival who remembers what you did.
A crew of three with trust meters and perks. Push someone too far and they walk.
Six endings, depending on the title result, your karma, your crew and your rival.
